sources.news_title: White House confiscates press badges of CNN, MS NOW, Politico reporters
sources.text:
Sept. 19 (UPI) — White House reporters had their badges confiscated or deactivated Saturday after President Donald Trump announced a ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters on Friday.
Trump said he was making the ban on Truth Social Friday, saying it was because of their “constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS.”
Trump, whose approval rating recently hit historic lows, told reporters Friday in the Oval Office that he didn’t like how the outlets covered him.
“There’s something wrong with a country that can allow people to write purposely negative stories,” Trump said. “Now, if they want to write them, that’s fine, but I don’t have to let them into my — into the people’s house.”
White House Communications Director said in an email Saturday that Trump’s senior staff support the move, The New York Times reported.
“We all fully support his decision to hold Fake News accountable for their continued lies,” he wrote.
Bruce D. Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, said the ban won’t stand up in court.
“A ban like this would be flatly unconstitutional,” he said in a statement. “The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can’t ban others because it doesn’t like their reporting. This is textbook viewpoint discrimination and will be quickly struck down by the courts if challenged.”
MS NOW correspondent Akayla Gardner said her White House-issued access badge failed to work on Saturday, The Times reported.
“The officer asked me to hand over my badge; he said that it was disabled,” Gardner said. “I asked why I could not get inside; he said it was above him.”
CNN correspondent Betsy Klein described a similar experience about an hour later. She said a White House security officer, whom she has known for years, told her that her badge had been deactivated.
“I asked if he had any more details he could share with me,” Klein said in an on-air interview. “He said I should be referred to the White House press office for more information.”
Politico reporter Cheyenne Haslett was also denied access.
Politico reported that most of the White House staff were surprised by the move. The press department, however, took it seriously.
“It’s real and permanent as far as POTUS is concerned,” an aide said Friday.
MS NOW made a statement saying its reporters were denied access to the White House.
“MS NOW intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy,” the statement said.
CNN said in a statement, “We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do our reporting without hindrance or interference from the government and this ban is an illegal assault on this fundamental right. We will not be deflected from our duty to hold the government and other public bodies to account, and we will continue to report on the actions and processes of this administration without fear or favor.”
Politico also posted a statement on X. It said reporter Cheyenne Haslett was denied access by the Secret Service, and her pass was taken away.
“We stand by her and all reporters here covering the White House. … We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights,” the statement said.

sources.news_title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico Reporters Barred From White House as Press Badges Are Revoked
sources.text:
Reporters for CNN, MS NOW and Politico were turned away from the White House and had press credentials disabled or confiscated Saturday, one day after President Donald Trump announced the three news organizations were banned over coverage he characterized as false.
By yourNEWS Media Newsroom.
Journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico were denied entry to the White House grounds Saturday and had press credentials revoked or confiscated as the Trump administration began enforcing President Donald Trump’s newly announced ban on the three news organizations.
The access restrictions took effect Sept. 19, one day after Trump declared that the outlets would no longer be permitted at the White House because of what he characterized as years of inaccurate reporting. Reporters from all three organizations encountered the restrictions when attempting to enter the complex Saturday.
Trump announced the decision Sept. 18 on Truth Social, writing that he was, effective immediately, banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!”
“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America. Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow,” Trump added.
The president did not cite a specific article or broadcast as the reason for the action, according to reporting on the announcement.
MS NOW White House correspondent Akayla Gardner said she was able to pass through earlier security checkpoints Saturday morning before discovering at another entrance that her credential had been disabled.
“Once I was inside where we have magnetometers, I attempted to scan my badge, which we have to do to be able to get into the White House grounds,” Gardner said during a live MS NOW broadcast.
“It did not work. There was a red beeping light, and so the officer asked me to hand over my badge. He said that it was disabled.”
Gardner said the officer could not provide a specific explanation and told her the decision “was above him.”
Security personnel then took Gardner’s badge and the credential belonging to an MS NOW photographer, she said. An MS NOW producer was still able to enter with a credential that remained active.
MS NOW responded by saying it intends to challenge the restrictions.
“The White House belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars,” MS NOW stated.
The network said it plans to take “any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights” and indicated that its journalists would continue covering the administration despite the loss of White House access.
CNN senior White House reporter Betsy Klein also attempted to enter the grounds Saturday and was denied access. CNN said her credential had been revoked.
“We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do our reporting without hindrance or interference from the government and this ban is an illegal assault on this fundamental right,” CNN said in a statement Saturday.
The network said it will “continue to report on the actions and processes of this administration without fear or favor.”
Politico encountered the same restriction when White House reporter Cheyenne Haslett arrived at the complex.
Politico Editor-in-Chief Jonathan Greenberger said in the publication’s Playbook newsletter that Haslett was denied entry and her credential was confiscated.
“Secret Service denied her entry to the complex and confiscated the pass that allows her access to the White House,” the statement read.
“We stand by her and all reporters here covering the White House. As we said yesterday, we will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights.”
Reports and photographs Saturday showed Gardner, Klein and Haslett outside the White House after being denied entry.
The White House Correspondents’ Association also objected to the administration’s decision.
Association President Jacqui Heinrich, a senior White House correspondent for Fox News Channel, said the government should not base White House press access on whether the president approves of an organization’s coverage.
“The Constitution protects the freedom of the press from government interference,” Heinrich said in a Sept. 19 statement.
“That protection does not depend on whether the president likes a news organization’s coverage, agrees with its reporting, or approves of the questions its journalists ask.”
The three outlets’ statements and Heinrich’s comments frame the dispute as a First Amendment matter. Trump, by contrast, has said the restrictions are a response to reporting he considers false. Whether the new restrictions comply with constitutional requirements could ultimately become a matter for the courts if the affected organizations pursue litigation.
Existing federal appellate precedent has addressed the procedures surrounding White House press credentials.
In the 1977 case Sherrill v. Knight, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit held that once the White House makes press facilities available to journalists, access cannot be denied arbitrarily or for less than compelling reasons. The court also required notice, an opportunity to respond and a final written explanation when a White House press credential is denied for security reasons.
The latest confrontation also follows a separate dispute between the Trump administration and The Associated Press in 2025.
The White House restricted AP access to certain presidential events after the news organization declined to adopt “Gulf of America” as its exclusive terminology for the body of water historically known as the Gulf of Mexico.
A federal judge subsequently ordered the White House to restore AP access while litigation continued, finding that the government could not punish a news organization based on its viewpoint.
Saturday’s action against CNN, MS NOW and Politico goes beyond a dispute over access to an individual event. Reporters from all three organizations said their regular credentials had been disabled or confiscated when they attempted to enter the White House complex.
Trump also indicated that the restrictions may not end with those three organizations, writing that “Other Fake News Media Outlets” could follow.
For now, CNN, MS NOW and Politico say they intend to continue covering the administration while challenging the loss of White House access, setting up another dispute over the extent of presidential authority to determine which credentialed journalists may report from inside the White House complex.

Journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico had their badges confiscated when they attempted to enter the White House grounds today, a stark escalation in President Donald Trump’s battles with the news media that sets up a significant legal and constitutional clash.
Trump has sued, subpoenaed and threatened the press corps that reports on him. But his decision to bar those three news outlets, announced in a Truth Social post Friday, was so abrupt that it caught some administration officials off guard, including aides in the press office, according to three people who were told about the conversations.
First Amendment experts condemned Trump’s ban as unconstitutional and said that it was unlikely to survive a court challenge. Affected outlets pledged to defend their legal rights. And CNN’s rival television networks were discussing how to proceed in the event that CNN was still banned this coming week.
It remained unclear what had prompted Trump to issue his insult-laden Truth Social post, which he published while Susie Wiles, his chief of staff, was out of town.
Steven Cheung, the White House communications director, said in an email today that members of Trump’s senior staff were with him at the time he published the Truth Social post. “We all fully support his decision to hold Fake News accountable for their continued lies,” he wrote.

Five networks — ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News — rotate as the designated TV crew for presidential events, sharing the financial costs. CNN is scheduled to provide coverage for Trump’s visit to the U.N. General Assembly in New York this coming week.
If the other networks refused to substitute for CNN, then Trump would be left without a mainstream television crew covering his trip on Air Force One or his U.N. appearances.
There is precedent for this kind of collective action: In 2009, the major networks balked when the Obama administration attempted to bar Fox News from participating in a Treasury Department event; the administration backed down.
A confrontation Monday, when CNN’s pooling duties begin, could also be avoided if an affected news outlet were to sue, and a judge were to issue a temporary order to suspend Trump’s ban.

The gloves are now all the way off between the media and President Donald Trump in the fight over press freedoms.
Trump took to his social media platform Friday afternoon, Sept. 18, to announce he’s banning certain media outlets from the White House, a clear violation of the U.S. Constitution.
He’s taking the steps just six weeks ahead of the midterm elections as his approval rating continues to tank. Opponents say it’s Trump’s way of trying to control the narrative and limit bad press.
“I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW (who recently changed their name from MSNBC due to lack of viewership and credibility!), and Politico … from the White House as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!,” Trump wrote in the post.
The president went on to accuse the outlets of constantly writing “FICTION and LIES” when they cover him and his administration.
Later, Trump took questions from reporters in the Oval Office, who asked him about his plans to ban the news outlets.
“Every president takes an oath to uphold the Constitution, which includes the First Amendment,” the reporter began.
But Trump interrupted, “Yeah, I do too, much more so than you,” he sputtered.
“How do you justify this?” she questioned.
It’s amazing Trump even heard the question because he continued talking over the reporter.
“Because they’re fake news, and you get so tired of reading and seeing fake news. When you look at CNN, it’s just fake. That’s why their ratings are no good. When you look at MSNOW, which used to be MSNBC … it’s fake news. It’s fake news,” he insisted.
As a reporter tried to ask a follow-up, Trump continued talking over her, “Excuse me, excuse me.”
He went on to accuse Politico of writing “fake” stories, too. “So, there’s a lot of news. There may be others to join ’em, and maybe they can better, and we’d like to have them back in,” he groused.
Trump went on to continue bashing CNN. “You know how fake their reporting is.”
Saturday morning, CNN said its journalists were denied access to the White House grounds. They say the move, however, will not deter them from doing their job.
“CNN’s mission to report on the U.S. government will continue regardless of any attempts to restrict physical access to the White House and other government buildings, or any other attempts to impede our journalism,” the network said.
MSNOW journalists also had to report from outside the White House this morning after officials deactivated their passes.
The outlet says it “intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy.”
Politico also issued a statement saying the outlet “will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones. We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them.”
Secret service also denied their reporter, Cheyenne Haslett, access.
Trump has continually scuffled with the press since retaking the White House in early 2025. He banned The Associated Press from the Oval Office, Air Force One, and other events. It happened after they refused to call the Gulf of Mexico the “Gulf of America” after Trump renamed it by executive order.
He has also taken legal action against other outlets, including The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times, and the BBC. He has also threatened to revoke other networks’ FCC operating licenses.
He’s prioritized right-wing networks in the press room. And he’s constantly calling female journalists names when he doesn’t like their questions.
The AP reported that Trump’s action amounts to “viewpoint discrimination.” That’s when the government singles out “specific media outlets for the content of what they say or publish.” The principle is also at the center of many of the court cases focusing on how the president has treated the media.
“Someone needs to explain to President Trump how the First Amendment works,” PEN America’s Tim Richardson told the AP. “As we’ve seen time and time again, this administration’s hostility toward the press is never about the accuracy of news stories, but about its inability to withstand scrutiny of its actions.”
Social media exploded in anger over Trump’s threats.
“We’ve never had such an insecure little b–ch in the Oval Office. He couldn’t be any more pathetic,” a furious X user proclaimed.
Others agreed. “I don’t comment, ever. But that is changing now. The man who is occupying the White House is a psycho. He is seeking retribution on the entire country. He is a pathetic man child. He is deliberately destroying everything this country was built on. He should be be banned!”
A Threads user joined in. “They hurt his feelings so a little more further down the fascist pipeline we go.”
Commenter Maya MP used one word to describe Trump’s actions against the news media. “Dictator.”

Reporters locked out of White House grounds as Trump’s ban takes effect
Washington: Journalists from three major news organisations, including cable news channel CNN, were locked out of the White House grounds and had their passes seized after President Donald Trump banned them because he dislikes their journalism.
CNN’s Betsy Klein, MS NOW’s Akayla Gardner and Politico’s Cheyenne Haslett were reporting from the streets outside the White House on Saturday (US time) after failing to gain entry to their usual on-site offices.
It came the day after Trump declared he was permanently banning the three outlets because they produced “purposely negative stories”, in a dramatic and potentially unconstitutional escalation of his war against the media, which he labels “fake news”.
The affected outlets are expected to launch a legal challenge imminently. Trump’s move also triggered broad condemnation from across the media sector, including the White House Correspondents’ Association (WHCA), the Associated Press and The New York Times.
All three outlets reported that their staffers’ press passes were confiscated by Secret Service agents when they attempted to enter the White House grounds on Saturday morning. MS NOW said one of its producers was still able to enter the premises, however.
CNN’s Klein was broadcasting from the corner of 17th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue on Saturday. “We are going to continue to do our job whether it’s inside the White House grounds or right here at this intersection,” she said. “We can do our job anywhere.”
In a statement, CNN said its mission to report on the US government would continue regardless of attempts to restrict physical access to the White House or other government buildings.
“We have a right under the US Constitution to do our reporting without hindrance or interference from the government, and this ban is an illegal assault on this fundamental right,” the network said.
Jacqui Heinrich, the WHCA president and a White House correspondent for News Corp’s Fox News, said the revocation of access was a violation of the First Amendment and called for its immediate reversal.
“The implications extend beyond these organisations: a standard used to exclude one news outlet because of its coverage could be applied to any outlet in the future,” Heinrich said.
“The American people, through a free and independent press, must be able to scrutinise those elected to power, regardless of whether government officials view it favourably.
“That’s why courts have repeatedly held that once the White House provides access to journalists, it cannot deny that access arbitrarily or based on the content of their reporting.”
Trump signalled on Friday that he expected the ban to be challenged in court, and that he believed the result might depend on the particular judge.
“I don’t think that a court should allow fake news to be written day after day after day,” he said. “I think that somebody has a right to keep them away.”
There was no particular trigger for the sudden ban, Trump said. “It’s really just cumulative stories over the last few years. You get sick of it.”
The unprecedented ban is an escalation of Trump’s long-standing animosity towards the media, which he has deployed in multiple elections to paint himself as a victim of so-called “fake news”.
It comes just weeks before the midterm election, and in the absence of a White House press secretary. Karoline Leavitt departed the role last month and has not been replaced.
Politico reported the decision was made while White House chief-of-staff Susie Wiles was out of town, and blindsided the rest of the press office on Friday afternoon.
But there have been several precursors to a move of this magnitude. Last year, Trump attempted to ban the Associated Press from the Oval Office after it declined to rename the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America, in line with his executive order.
And most mainstream news outlets no longer maintain a presence at the Pentagon after the Department of Defence required them to sign onerous new conditions. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the outlets had “chosen to self-deport”.
Jose Zamora, American regional director at the Committee to Protect Journalists, said Trump’s arbitrary ban on the three outlets illustrated that he was not interested in a free press or protecting constitutional rights.
“His administration’s weaponisation of government agencies and access to target critical coverage must end, and journalists must be allowed to do their jobs free from retaliation,” Zamora said.
Trump said other news outlets could be banned, too, and named The New York Times and The Washington Post among those he particularly disliked.
A spokesman for the Times, Charlie Stadtlander, said the paper stood in solidarity with the other organisations being unfairly targeted by the president.

It also said journalists denied credentials must receive notice of the factual basis, an opportunity to respond, and a final written explanation.
It is not yet clear what legal recourse CNN, MS NOW or Politico may pursue, or how courts would apply Sherrill to the administration’s decision to revoke existing credentials.
Al Jazeera’s Alan Fisher reported from Washington, DC, on Friday that Trump’s ban will likely be challenged soon.
“The United States has the First Amendment [of its Constitution] that says the government cannot restrict access to this sort of thing,” he said.
Press freedom advocates are watching closely.
Jameel Jaffer, executive director of the Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University, said in a news release that the move raises constitutional concerns.
“If President Trump means to expel these news organizations from the White House press pool, his action is doubly unconstitutional because the press pool is a ‘public forum’ under the First Amendment, which means the president can’t exclude journalists from it on the basis of their viewpoints,” Jaffer said.
The fight over access could now become a broader test of the limits on the White House’s ability to control which journalists can cover the administration.
“It’s difficult to imagine a more blatant violation of the First Amendment than Trump banning news outlets from the People’s House for criticizing the government,” said Seth Stern, chief of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation. “It’s also hard to imagine a dumber move.”

sources.text:
Reporters from CNN, MS Now and Politico were barred from the White House
(AP) — Reporters from three major news organizations — CNN, MS NOW and Politico — were denied access to the White House on Saturday, a day after President Donald Trump said he was barring them because of reporting he found to be “fake news.”
The actions were a clear escalation of Trump’s long-running efforts — in the courts and through administrative action — to restrict news coverage by journalists he finds objectionable, and the latest test of First Amendment protections in the United States. Trump had said Friday he would ban all three outlets because of coverage he disliked.
White House reporters from the two cable networks — Betsy Klein of CNN and Akayla Gardner of MS NOW — both went live to report they’d been turned away when arriving for their jobs at the White House. Soon after, Politico said its White House reporter Cheyenne Haslett was also denied entry and had her badge confiscated.
Politico Editor-in-Chief Jonathan Greenberger said in a statement to the Politico newsroom: “We stand by her and all reporters here covering the White House. … We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights.”
CNN and MS NOW issued similar statements. “We will not be deflected from our duty to hold the government and other public bodies to account,” CNN said.
“The White House belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars,” MS NOW said in its statement. “MS NOW intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy.”’
In his second term, Trump and his administration have upped the ante and punished certain media outlets, both in the courtroom and through regulatory action. Trump has also lashed out at individual reporters in person or over social media, sometimes in strikingly personal terms — insulting them in briefings, or in his recent speech at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner.
CNN and MS NOW correspondents are turned away
Network correspondents are usually present on the weekends when the president is in Washington or at nearby Camp David. Trump is at the presidential retreat in Maryland this weekend.
MS NOW’s Gardner reported that she had walked through two gates successfully, but once she got to where her badge needed to be scanned, an officer told her it was disabled and asked her to hand it over. He said the decision “was above him,” she reported. An MS NOW producer was able to get in, but a photographer’s badge was also disabled, Gardner said.
Klein, senior White House reporter at CNN, also said her badge had been deactivated. It was confiscated, and she was handed back the clear plastic case. She said she was referred to the White House press office for further information.
Amy Kristin Sanders, a professor at Penn State University and an expert in media law, said it has “become pretty clear that this administration is not interested in playing by traditional First Amendment rules and norms.
“The second Trump administration’s efforts to crack down on press freedom and delegitimize independent journalism far exceed those of any other modern American president,” Sanders said. “It is not an exaggeration to say his hostile actions toward news organizations and individual reporters have a chilling effect on freedom of expression around the world.”
CNN media analyst Brian Stelter called the move “a direct threat to press freedom in the United States.”
“It’s so much bigger than CNN,” Stelter said. “This is a free speech test in America.”
Trump calls these and other outlets ‘fake news’
The president wrote on his social media site Friday that effective immediately, “I am banning” CNN, MS NOW and Politico “from the White House as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” Minutes later, speaking at an event in the Oval Office, Trump was asked to explain his statement.
“Because they’re fake news,” he said. “You get so tired of reading and seeing fake news. When you look at CNN, it’s just fake. That’s why their ratings are no good. When you look at MS NOW … , it’s fake news.”
“And when you look at Politico … the stories they wrote are fake. So there’s a lot of news and there may be others to join them, and maybe they can get better,” he said. “But our country has to have honest news.”
The move follows the president’s decision last year to bar Associated Press reporters from the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events in retaliation for the news outlet’s decision not to follow his lead in changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico, which lies partially in Mexican and other waters. The AP said that it would note when appropriate that Trump had ordered it renamed the “Gulf of America.”
The AP filed suit and the case is ongoing. Since returning to office, Trump has pursued other legal action against a variety of different outlets, including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the BBC. His administration is also involved in a long-simmering confrontation involving ABC over renewal of its broadcast licenses.
The AP said Saturday it supported the news organizations banned this week. In a statement, it said: “No news organization — or person — should be retaliated against by the government over the words they use.”

The newly-banned organizations will surely challenge this measure in court, and unless our constitutional order has completely fallen apart, they’ll likely win. But that doesn’t erase the damage — the distraction, cost, and chaos that this kind of thing will cause.

CNN — an outlet long targeted by Trump — said its "mission to report on the US government will continue regardless of any attempts to restrict physical access to the White House and other government buildings, or any other attempts to impede our journalism".
"We will not be deflected from our duty to hold the government and other public bodies to account, and we will continue to report on the actions and processes of this administration without fear or favor," the news network added. "CNN stands fully behind our White House team."
First Amendment rights
MS NOW — a left-leaning channel formerly attached to NBC — said it "intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy", referring to the US constitution's guarantee of a free press.

"The White House belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars," the network added.

Politico’s communications team disputed his claim that the publication “received government subsidies”, saying the allegation had been "thoroughly debunked".
“POLITICO will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones. We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them,” an online post said.

sources.text:
Trump said on Truth Social Sept. 18 that he was, effective immediately, banning CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!”
The president added: “Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America. Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow.”
Akayla Gardner, a White House correspondent for MS NOW, said that her press pass was revoked at the third gate she passed through to enter the grounds on Saturday morning.
“Once I was inside where we have magnetometers, I attempted to scan my badge, which we have to do to be able to get into the White House grounds,” Gardner said during a live broadcast on MS NOW.
“It did not work. There was a red beeping light, and so the officer asked me to hand over my badge. He said that it was disabled.”
Gardner said the officer on duty wasn’t able to explain specifically why her badge did not work, allegedly saying the decision “was above him.”
Gardner’s badge and her photographer’s badge were both then “taken” away from them by security, she said. However, an MS NOW producer’s pass was approved, and the employee was still able to go inside, Gardner said.
MS NOW defended its team and newsroom in a statement on Saturday morning, saying the media channel plans to take “any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights” as journalists in a democracy.
“The White House belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars,” MS NOW stated on social media.
The outlet stated that it will continue reporting on the Trump administration, even if its reporters are not allowed on White House grounds.
CNN’s reporter Betsy Klein was also denied access and had her press pass revoked.
“We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do our reporting without hindrance or interference from the government and this ban is an illegal assault on this fundamental right,” a statement by CNN read on Saturday.
CNN stated that it will “continue to report on the actions and processes of this administration without fear or favor.”
POLITICO editor-in-chief Jonathan Greenberger shared in the publication’s daily newsletter Playbook that the company’s White House reporter, Cheyenne Haslett, was also locked out on Saturday.
“Secret Service denied her entry to the complex and confiscated the pass that allows her access to the White House,” the statement read.
“We stand by her and all reporters here covering the White House. As we said yesterday, we will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights.”
White House Correspondents’ Association president Jacqui Heinrich, a Senior White House Correspondent for Fox News Channel, accused the White House of singling out CNN, MS NOW and Politico for “doing their jobs.”
“The Constitution protects the freedom of the press from government interference,” Heinrich wrote in a statement on Sept. 19.
“That protection does not depend on whether the president likes a news organization’s coverage, agrees with its reporting, or approves of the questions its journalists ask.”

CNN, MS NOW and Politico denied access to White House
September 19, 2026
News outlets CNN, MS NOW and Politico on Saturday signaled they would take legal action after their journalists were denied access to the White House grounds earlier in the day.
It comes a day after US President Donald Trump announced he would ban the three news outlets from 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue in a row over their coverage of his presidency.
Trump has accused the media of "fake news" over their often critical coverage of his second term in office.
Experts say the bans conflict with the United States Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech and press freedom.
What did CNN, MS NOW and Politico say?
CNN reported that its journalist Betsy Klein was denied access at the White House on Saturday morning and her press pass was seized.
"CNN’s mission to report on the U.S. government will continue regardless of any attempts to restrict physical access to the White House and other government buildings, or any other attempts to impede our journalism,” a statement from the channel said.
“We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do our reporting without hindrance or interference from the government and this ban is an illegal assault on this fundamental right."
Meanwhile, the left-leaning MS NOW, whose journalists were also turned away from the White House grounds on Saturday, said in a statement that it would challenge Trump's ban.
"The White House belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars,” the network said. "MS NOW intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy.”

La Casa Blanca niega el acceso a CNN, a MS NOW y a Politico tras el “veto” de Trump
Por Brian Stelter, CNN
A la reportera de CNN Betsy Klein se le negó el acceso a la Casa Blanca este sábado por la mañana y se le confiscó su credencial de prensa, un día después de que el presidente Donald Trump anunciara que “vetaba” a CNN, MS NOW y Politico.
Los expertos en la Primera Enmienda afirman que esta medida es inconstitucional.
A un reportero de Politico y a un reportero y un fotógrafo de MS NOW también se les negó el acceso al recinto de la Casa Blanca cuando llegaron a trabajar el sábado por la mañana.
Las tres organizaciones de noticias indicaron que emprenderán acciones legales para defender los derechos de sus reporteros.
“Esta mañana, se negó a los periodistas de CNN el acceso al recinto de la Casa Blanca. La misión de CNN de informar sobre el Gobierno de EE.UU. continuará independientemente de cualquier intento de restringir el acceso físico a la Casa Blanca y a otros edificios gubernamentales, o de cualquier otro intento de obstaculizar nuestro periodismo”, declaró CNN en un comunicado. “Tenemos derecho, según la Constitución de EE.UU., a realizar nuestra labor informativa sin trabas ni interferencias del gobierno, y esta prohibición constituye un ataque ilegal a este derecho fundamental”.
Klein informó que un agente del Servicio Secreto le dijo que su credencial de prensa había sido desactivada.
“Le pregunté si podía explicarme por qué se había desactivado”, relató Klein al aire a Kasie Hunt, de la CNN, este sábado por la mañana. “Dijo que no tenía más información. Le pregunté una vez más si tenía algún detalle adicional que pudiera compartir conmigo, y respondió que debía dirigirme a la Oficina de Prensa de la Casa Blanca”.
La corresponsal de MS NOW, Akayla Gardner, relató algo similar: “Un agente me pidió que entregara mi credencial. Dijo que estaba desactivada. Pregunté por qué no podía entrar. Respondió que el asunto escapaba a su competencia”.
Gardner contó lo sucedido en una transmisión en directo desde fuera del perímetro de la Casa Blanca.
Trump anunció el viernes por la tarde que CNN, MS NOW y Politico quedaban vetados “con efecto inmediato”, al tiempo que se quejaba de las noticias “falsas” (fake news), su frase habitual para desestimar la cobertura informativa desfavorable.
El anuncio tomó por sorpresa a algunos miembros del personal de la Casa Blanca. Los periodistas de los tres medios permanecieron en la Casa Blanca hasta la noche del viernes.
Sin embargo, al abandonar el recinto al final de la jornada, se preguntaban si sus credenciales de seguridad funcionarían la próxima vez; el incidente de MS NOW este sábado por la mañana empezó a responder a esa pregunta.
Gardner comentó que a su compañero fotógrafo también se le negó la entrada, pero una productora de MS NOW “pasó su credencial por el lector y esta funcionó. Pudo pasar y entrar en la Casa Blanca”.
Decenas de periodistas trabajan desde el complejo de la Casa Blanca en cualquier día dado.
MSNBC declaró este sábado por la mañana que la cadena “tiene la intención de tomar todas las medidas necesarias para defender nuestros derechos consagrados en la Primera Enmienda y el papel esencial del periodismo independiente en nuestra democracia. Respaldamos firmemente a nuestros presentadores, reporteros y a nuestra redacción. Seguiremos informando sobre el presidente, la administración y los temas que afectan al pueblo estadounidense”.
El viernes, Bruce D. Brown, presidente del Comité de Reporteros por la Libertad de Prensa (Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press), afirmó que “una prohibición de este tipo sería rotundamente inconstitucional”.
“La Primera Enmienda es clara: una vez que la Casa Blanca permite el acceso a algunos periodistas, no puede vetar a otros simplemente porque no le agrada su cobertura”, señaló Brown. “Esto es un caso de manual de discriminación por motivos de opinión y sería rápidamente anulado por los tribunales si se impugnara”.
Muchos comentaristas especularon que la “prohibición” del presidente era un intento de desviar la atención de una semana de titulares desfavorables a medida que se acercan las elecciones de mitad de mandato. Trump enfrenta actualmente una presión creciente debido a una guerra altamente impopular en Irán, así como al aumento de los precios de la gasolina y a la preocupación por el costo de vida.
Atacar a los medios de comunicación ha sido un elemento constante del discurso político de Trump durante una década, y una forma segura de ganarse el aplauso en los mítines del movimiento MAGA.
Sin embargo, en su segundo mandato, Trump ha intentado cada vez más convertir esas palabras en acciones, tomando medidas concretas para limitar el acceso de la prensa, aun cuando su Casa Blanca afirma ser la más transparente en la historia de Estados Unidos.
Clayton Weimers, CEO de Reporteros Sin Fronteras para América del Norte, declaró: “El presidente vuelve a lanzar mentiras sobre las ‘noticias falsas’ (fake news) para intentar controlar quién informa sobre él y desde dónde”.
“El acceso de la prensa no es un privilegio para los periodistas”, afirmó Weimers. “Es un derecho para garantizar que el pueblo estadounidense pueda recibir información de manera independiente”.

A CNN statement said the network “will not be deflected from our duty to hold the government and other public bodies to account.”
And MS NOW said it “intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy.”
In his second term, Trump and his administration have upped the ante and punished certain media outlets, both in the courtroom and through regulatory action. The WHCA’s president, Jacqui Heinrich, called on the administration to immediately restore the three outlets’ access. “The implications extend beyond these organizations: a standard used to exclude one news outlet because of its coverage could be applied to any outlet in the future,” Heinrich said. “The American people, through a free and independent press, must be able to scrutinize those elected to power, regardless of whether government officials view it favorably.”

Network correspondents are usually present on the weekends when the president is in Washington or at nearby Camp David. Trump is at the presidential retreat in Maryland this weekend.

He said the decision “was above him,” she reported. An MS NOW producer was able to get in, but a photographer’s badge was also disabled, Gardner said.
Klein, senior White House reporter at CNN, also said her badge had been deactivated. It was confiscated, and she was handed back the clear plastic case. She said she was referred to the White House press office for further information.
Amy Kristin Sanders, a professor at Penn State University and an expert in media law, said it has “become pretty clear that this administration is not interested in playing by traditional First Amendment rules and norms.”
“The second Trump administration’s efforts to crack down on press freedom and delegitimize independent journalism far exceed those of any other modern American president,” Sanders said. “It is not an exaggeration to say his hostile actions toward news organizations and individual reporters have a chilling effect on freedom of expression around the world.”
CNN media analyst Brian Stelter called the move “a direct threat to press freedom in the United States.”
“It’s so much bigger than CNN,” Stelter said. “This is a free speech test in America.”

The president wrote on his social media site Friday that effective immediately, “I am banning” CNN, MS NOW and Politico “from the White House as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” Minutes later, speaking at an event in the Oval Office, Trump was asked to explain his statement.
“Because they’re fake news,” he said. “You get so tired of reading and seeing fake news. When you look at CNN, it’s just fake. That’s why their ratings are no good. When you look at MS NOW … , it’s fake news.”
“And when you look at Politico ... the stories they wrote are fake. So there’s a lot of news and there may be others to join them, and maybe they can get better,” he said. “But our country has to have honest news.”
The move follows the president’s decision last year to bar Associated Press reporters from the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events in retaliation for the news outlet’s decision not to follow his lead in changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico, which lies partially in Mexican and other waters. The AP said that it would note when appropriate that Trump had ordered it renamed the “Gulf of America.”
The AP filed suit and the case is ongoing. Since returning to office, Trump has pursued other legal action against a variety of different outlets, including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the BBC. His administration is also involved in a long-simmering confrontation involving ABC over renewal of its broadcast licenses.
The AP said Saturday it supported the news organizations banned this week. In a statement, the news cooperative said: “No news organization — or person — should be retaliated against by the government over the words they use.”
___
Associated Press journalist Mike Householder contributed.

MS NOW Journalists Denied White House Access After Trump Ban
Journalists from MS NOW were turned away from the White House grounds on Saturday, a day after President Donald Trump announced plans to bar the network, CNN and Politico from the complex.
MS NOW confirmed that its reporters were denied entry as the administration moved to enforce Trump’s announcement, which he made on Friday and linked to what he described as inaccurate and unfavourable coverage.
Trump had accused the three organisations of publishing what he called “fake news” and said the restrictions would take effect immediately. On Friday afternoon, journalists from the targeted outlets were still working from the White House grounds.
MS NOW said it would defend its journalists and challenge any attempt to restrict its reporting rights.
“The White House belongs to the American people,” the network said in a statement, adding that it intended to take steps to protect what it described as its First Amendment rights and the role of independent journalism.
It remained unclear on Saturday whether CNN reporters had also been prevented from entering the White House grounds. Politico journalists are generally not stationed at the complex on Saturdays.
Trump’s announcement has prompted renewed debate over presidential control of media access and constitutional protections for journalists. Legal experts and press organisations have questioned whether the government can exclude news organisations because of dissatisfaction with their reporting.
The White House has not publicly provided detailed procedures explaining how the newly announced restrictions will be applied.
